research_goldbach.touch_once_checkbox: One touch per n is enough (check existence only, don't count all sums)
research_goldbach.hint: Enter any integer n -- Pmax is derived automatically as the largest prime <= n. Checks every even number in [4, 2*Pmax] for a decomposition into a sum of two primes (windowCovered from Structural.lean). "Touch once" mode only searches for existence (stops at the first witness found) -- the paper's active line of proof. "All combinations" mode computes the full repCount(n) for every even number -- the counting framing, kept in the formalization only for comparison, since it inherits the parity problem.
research_goldbach.lean_repo_link: Lean 4 formalization of this tab on GitHub (proofs, zero "sorry") →
research_goldbach.viz_range_hint: "to" plays the old n field's role -- Pmax (largest prime <= to) is derived from it, and it's also the scan's own upper bound. "from" defaults to 4, but can be changed -- it must be >=4 and at least 2 less than "to" (so at least one even number fits in the range). A narrower range scans faster for large values.

research_goldbach.viz_hint: Draws the window [4, Pmax+2] (Pmax = largest prime <= n) -- exactly the range the Lean lemma "additiveSelfContained_of_hasGoldbachRep" proves unconditionally. Primes are read from storage (across every floor needed), not recomputed. Both p and q are required <= Pmax here -- there is no separate "q may be new" mode anymore, this is the one, more general window.

research_goldbach.viz_status_shown: Showing window for n={n} (Pmax={pmax}). Change n above and check again.
research_goldbach.viz_subheader: The old base (blue, primes <= Pmax) supplies BOTH summands (p and q) for EVERY even number shown below -- window narrowed to [4, Pmax+2], because that's exactly the range where Lean (additiveSelfContained_of_hasGoldbachRep, SelfContainment.lean) proves unconditionally: if any representation of n exists at all, both summands are <= Pmax.
research_goldbach.viz_q_new_note: q > Pmax -- not needed for p
research_goldbach.viz_legend_new_q: both summands (p and q) share the same blue -- here BOTH must be <= Pmax, that's a proven requirement (Lean), not just information
research_goldbach.viz_summary_covered: Segment covered -- all {segment_size} new even numbers built from the old base alone.
research_goldbach.error_decompose_no_win: Check the window first (the "Sprawdz okno" button above) to establish a Pmax to compare against.
research_goldbach.error_decompose_must_b: The number to decompose must be even and >= 4.
research_goldbach.decompose_verdict_yes: buildableFromBase(Pmax={pmax}) [Lean, Constructive.lean] CONFIRMED: every one of the {count} pairs has p <= Pmax -- that is exactly Lean's own criterion (exists p q, p <= B and ...), which only ever bounds p, never q. For n inside the window [4, 2*Pmax] this is a PROVEN arithmetic fact (p <= n/2 <= Pmax), not just an observation.
research_goldbach.decompose_verdict_no: buildableFromBase(Pmax={pmax}) [Lean, Constructive.lean] NOT confirmed -- this number lies OUTSIDE the window [4, 2*Pmax] for this Pmax, so the p <= n/2 <= Pmax proof doesn't apply here; none of the {count} pairs has p <= Pmax.

const_records.hint: Scans THIS project's OWN storage (constellations/kK/variantID/, not pzktupel.de) for the selected k -- shows the smallest offset found per floor and variant. The "Floor from/to" fields (optional, leave blank for no bound) limit the scan to a specific floor range instead of the whole storage -- useful when storage is large and the full table gets unreadable. PDF/CSV export includes every individual hit (not just the smallest offset) for the currently displayed floor range. quick.intro: Enter a floor or a number range to generate -- the app will translate it into the window width and window count in the form below (window width capped at 10,000,000).
quick.hint_floor: If the floor doesn't exist yet, it will be created. Width is a multiple of 10 million (1 = 10M, max 1000 = 10B) -- the requested amount is always rounded up to whole windows, on-disk files stay the same predictable size. Empty starting point = continue from the last existing file (then type the Floor field yourself); a given starting point determines the floor for you (the field becomes read-only) and sets a LITERAL target -- the app checks whether [starting point, starting point + width) is already in storage and reports that instead of regenerating it; if only part is missing, it generates just that part.
quick.hint_range: Both fields are required, From cannot be greater than or equal to To, minimum value for From is 0. Python-style formats allowed, e.g. 10**5. The range is rounded out to whole windows: From rounded down, To rounded up to the nearest multiple of 10,000,000 (e.g. 12M..309M -> 10M..310M). Must fit within a single floor -- the engine generates one floor at a time. If the given range is already fully in storage, the app will say so; if only partially, it will generate the missing part (from the last existing file through the end of the requested range).
quick.explore_auto_floor_empty: Nothing has been generated yet anywhere in this database -- type a floor yourself to start exploring one.
quick.hint_explore: Leave Floor blank (or click its own "Auto (highest floor)" button, which fills it in explicitly) to continue from wherever the deepest generated data in the whole database currently sits -- re-detected fresh every time, so pressing Generate repeatedly with nothing typed keeps extending whatever is genuinely deepest right now. Type a floor yourself to explore a specific one instead; this mode only ever continues an EXISTING floor (it never creates a new one), so a completely empty database still needs one typed by hand. A low floor (0-6, 0 is a real floor here, not a stand-in for blank) is a small, fixed range shared by all of them together: if it isn't fully generated yet, one click fills it completely (Iterations/Width don't apply to it) and stops there; if it's ALREADY fully generated, this mode automatically rolls forward to floor 7 instead and continues using the Iterations/Width you asked for -- there's nothing left below floor 7 to explore, ever. Width is a multiple of 10 million PER iteration (1 = 10M, max 1000 = 10B, same meaning as Floor only's) -- size it to the available RAM (see ITS OWN Auto button, further right). Number of iterations is how many times that width gets added in a row (max 100).
quick.hint_hybrid: Hybrid builds MAIN and the filter independently of storage. Floor and Width choose ordinary output windows; every iteration repeats that fixed block with one base. Existing files are skipped and gaps are filled without overwriting. Filter primes / stage is the visible k_adv parameter.
quick.hint_primesieve: Floor + From + Width, not From/To -- From is a literal starting point (like Floor mode's own Starting point field), Width is a multiple of 10 million added to it (same [1, 1000] meaning as Floor/Exploration mode's Width). Floor is independent of From -- type a floor and click Auto to fill From with wherever that floor's storage currently ends, without having to work out a huge resume number by hand; leaving From blank and just entering a Floor does the same thing automatically when you click Generate. Generation runs through libprimesieve's own primesieve_generate_primes() directly, with no batching/orchestrator of ours involved -- the fastest way to fill a range, within libprimesieve's own uint64 limit (up to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615). Requesting anything past that limit truncates the result to it; use Floor, Range, or Exploration mode instead for numbers beyond it (slower, but with no such ceiling).

research_goldbach.error_both_base_pmax_t: This window is only verified up to Pmax={ceiling} -- this n gives Pmax={pmax}, too large. Pick a smaller n.
quick.attribution_cudasieve: This mode calls CUDASieve, an independent open-source project by Curtis Seizert (github.com/curtisseizert/CUDASieve, GPLv3 license) directly, as a separate process -- never linked into this application. Requires an Nvidia GPU and building CUDASieve first via Settings > Updates.
quick.hint_cudasieve: Floor + From + Width, exactly like primesieve mode -- but this mode calls CUDASieve, a separate program that runs on the graphics card (build it first via Settings > Updates; requires an Nvidia GPU and the CUDA Toolkit inside WSL). CUDASieve cannot print individual primes below 2^40 (~1.0995 trillion) -- a request entirely below that value is rejected; use primesieve, Floor, Range, or Exploration mode instead. Floor is independent of From -- type a floor and click Auto to fill From with wherever that floor's storage currently ends (automatically raised to 2^40 if that floor is too low for this mode).
quick.cudasieve_auto_from_clamped: Floor {floor} is too low for cudasieve mode (it cannot print primes below 2^40). From has been set to {min_printable} -- the lowest value this mode can use.
quick.error_cudasieve_below_min: CUDASieve cannot print individual primes below 2^40 ({min_printable}) -- the entire requested range falls below that value. Use primesieve, Floor, Range, or Exploration mode instead.
quick.error_cudasieve_beyond_ceiling: The From value is already past CUDASieve's own uint64 limit ({max_stop}) -- this mode cannot generate anything up here. Use Floor, Range, or Exploration mode instead.
quick.note_cudasieve_ceiling: NOTE: part of this range is past CUDASieve's own uint64 limit ({max_stop}) -- the run will be truncated to that limit. Use Floor, Range, or Exploration mode instead for numbers above it (slower, but with no such ceiling).
settings.cudasieve_hint: CUDASieve is a separate, third-party GPU-accelerated sieve by Curtis Seizert (github.com/curtisseizert/CUDASieve), licensed under GNU GPLv3 -- NOT the same license as PrimeAtlas. It is never bundled with this project: installing clones and builds it fresh from its own repository into your WSL home folder, requires an Nvidia GPU and the CUDA Toolkit (nvcc), and is invoked as a separate process, never linked into this app. You will be shown its actual license text and must accept it before the build step runs. Usable only for floors at or above 10^13 (its own CLI does not print individual primes below 2^40).
settings.cudasieve_status_not_checked: CUDASieve: not checked yet -- click "Check status"
settings.cudasieve_status_cloned_not_bui: CUDASieve: downloaded to {path}, not built yet -- test `make`/nvcc manually in a WSL terminal there before installing further.
settings.cudasieve_status_no_gpu: CUDASieve: no Nvidia GPU detected in WSL (nvidia-smi not found) -- this engine cannot run here.
settings.cudasieve_status_no_nvcc: CUDASieve: Nvidia GPU detected, but the CUDA Toolkit (nvcc) is missing -- install it first, then retry.
settings.cudasieve_fetching_license: Cloning/updating CUDASieve and fetching its current License file...
settings.cudasieve_consent_intro: This is the ACTUAL, current License file just fetched from CUDASieve's own repository (github.com/curtisseizert/CUDASieve), by Curtis Seizert. It governs CUDASieve itself, not PrimeAtlas. Building it (next step, if you accept) compiles the source now on disk in your WSL home folder into a separate executable that PrimeAtlas will call as its own process -- it is never linked into this app.
settings.cudasieve_consent_declined: Declined -- CUDASieve was cloned but not built (source left on disk, harmless and unused).
settings.cudasieve_build_starting: Building CUDASieve (make) -- this can take a while...
settings.cudasieve_build_failed: Build failed (exit code: {code}). See the log above -- likely CUDA_DIR/GPU architecture flags in CUDASieve's own makefile need adjusting for your system.
wizard.title: PrimeAtlas -- environment setup
wizard.intro: PrimeAtlas runs its scripts inside WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux). Before continuing, Atlas will check whether WSL, the Ubuntu distribution, and required packages (numpy, libprimesieve) are already installed, and offer to install them if not.
wizard.status_installing: Installing missing components (this may take a few minutes)...
wizard.status_restart_required: A computer restart is required before continuing.
wizard.log_install_starting: Starting installation -- an Administrator (UAC) prompt will appear shortly.
wizard.log_restart_required: Windows components were enabled, but a computer restart is required. Relaunch PrimeAtlas after restarting -- the same setup will continue automatically.
settings.env_hint: Re-check whether WSL, the Ubuntu distribution, and required packages (numpy, libprimesieve) are still correctly installed -- useful if something got uninstalled or broken since the first-run check.
settings.env_status_not_checked: Not checked yet on this install.
rings.intro: Opens an interactive, GPU-driven visualization of prime rings around a chosen n -- a separate window (GLFW/OpenGL) launched as a subprocess, fed primes from the currently configured storage. Close that window anytime (Esc or the window's own close control) to return here.
rings.error_range_invalid: Range mode needs valid, non-negative From/To values.
rings.error_no_portal: No storage folder is configured (Settings tab).
rings.console_closed_error: Visualization process exited with an error (code {code}).
rings.status_paused: Ring visualization paused (window hidden) -- click Start / Resume to continue.
rings.console_paused: Visualization window hidden, process idling in the background -- playback, tempo, and audio will resume exactly where they left off.
rings.console_resumed: Visualization resumed -- window shown again, continuing without interruption.
rings.hud_panel_placeholder: (open a visualization to see live status here)
rings.audio_hint: Sound settings apply when opening a new visualization. Requires sounddevice.
